html:
Jordanes was a 6th-century official of the Eastern Roman Empire, of Gothic descent, who wrote a history of the Goths in Latin around 551.

His Getica shortens a longer Gothic history by Cassiodorus, now lost. It is the main surviving account of the early Goths and their split into Visigoths and Ostrogoths. It says the Goths came from "Scandza" in the north, and it tells the story of Attila and the battle of the Catalaunian Plains in 451.

Historians of the north value its lists of peoples. It names the Swedes, who sold fine furs to Rome, the Geats and northern hunters who may be the Saami. It gives one of the first accounts of the early Slavs, as the Sclaveni and Antes, and may name the Mordvins. How far to trust it is debated, since Jordanes wrote far from the events and flattered the Gothic royal house.
sum: Jordanes was a 6th-century official of the Eastern Roman Empire, of Gothic descent, who wrote a history of the Goths in Latin around 551.
